problem: Hilbert's fifteenth problem: put Schubert's enumerative calculus on a rigorous foundation
missing_details: Precise definition of the “geometrical numbers” computed by Schubert’s method
The principle of special position (conservation of number) as used by Schubert
The requirement to carry out elimination processes for equations of special form
The need to predict the degree of the resulting equations and the multiplicity of their solutions
Exact determination of the limits of validity of the enumerative calculus
refined_question: Establish rigorously, and with an exact determination of their limits of validity, the numerical invariants (geometrical numbers) computed by Schubert’s enumerative calculus—namely, those obtained via the principle of special position—by carrying out explicitly the necessary elimination processes for equations of special form so as to foresee both the degrees of the final equations and the multiplicities of their solutions.
justification: The given name indicates only that one must provide a rigorous foundation for Schubert’s enumerative calculus, but omits all details about which quantities are to be justified (the geometrical numbers), how they were computed (principle of special position), and the technical requirements (explicit elimination in special cases with control over degrees and multiplicities) as laid out in the original problem statement ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert%27s_fifteenth_problem)).
